results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 67 aligned summaries match the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in the spec's order (prediction p37-p39 before migrations p32-p36, as the spec orders the sections); the five callouts match no spec paragraph.

Only Introduction ¶3 was marked two_ideas (first governed subdomain / roadmap). The spec's p03 controlling idea is deliberately one transition idea: the chapter designs the tree the aggregate took as given, and names its route; the roadmap is that idea's elaboration, not a second claim.
Every body unit ties to a supporting claim C1-C6 through its aligned spec paragraph; no orphan paragraph found.

Each table has a lead-in or follow-up sentence stating what it shows (e.g. 'every system in the table below keys on it', 'Nine other concerns each needed a runbook step', 'Not every change needs a committee'); figures carry explanatory captions; each quotation (eBay, Amazon, Google, Auto Trader, Mercari) is followed by the point it supports.

results.draft_locus: In Practice: The Bikes Split at Veldmark ¶5
results.quote: Femke's Rotterdam city bike, sold in March 2027 and archived, illustrates the version rule from [[listing-aggregate]]
results.finding: Declared relationship is contrast, carrying over the live listings that moved and introducing an archived listing that did not. The opening sentence gives no contrast with the 410,000 live listings just reclassified and audited; it jumps to a new example of the version rule. Both flow readers felt the paragraph out of place in the reclassification subsection (see the flow result for this unit). A clause such as 'Archived listings did not move' would express the declared contrast.

results.quote: Part II keeps the listing small and has it reference governed subdomains by ID. The category is the first of them and the one that selects the contract for the rest.
results.finding: Flow A: 'I had to re-read this. "The rest" could mean the rest of the subdomains or the rest of the listing, and "governed subdomains" is not explained here.' Flow B (item 1) re-read the same sentence for the same ambiguity and called the roadmap paragraph dense. Name what 'the rest' refers to.

results.quote: Veldmark's 3,900 distinct attribute keys (field names), 41% of them used on fewer than 0.1% of listings, are partly a taxonomy symptom.
results.finding: Flow A: 'These figures appear here for the first time in the chapter, as though the reader already knew them. They felt imported from elsewhere.' Flow B (item 4): 'reads like a number carried in from another chapter, and it pulled me out of the bikes thread'. The statistic needs a set-up clause saying where it comes from (Veldmark's group-wide attribute count).

results.draft_locus: The Taxonomy as Versioned Reference Data ¶1
results.quote: Because the canonical tree changes only through releases, it is **reference data**
results.finding: Both readers paused on a causal link that reads backwards: the tree is reference data by what it is, not because it is released. Flow A: 'The reasoning seemed backwards to me... I paused on it'; Flow B (item 6): 'This causal link read oddly... I re-read it'. The spec's declared cause_effect introduces 'what a release is and what treating the tree as reference data requires', which the prose can state without making releases the cause of being reference data.

results.quote: Many internal nodes mapped to one Google category, each a broader mapping, lose nothing on output; one internal node mapped to several partner codes, each narrower, needs an attribute rule to decide.
results.finding: Flow A: 'I had to re-read this to work out which side "broader" and "narrower" describe and what the attribute rule decides.' Flow B (item 7): 'I needed two readings to keep the directions of "broader" and "narrower" straight'. Say what the attribute rule decides (which partner code a listing gets).

results.quote: A model trained on version 2027.10 cannot predict leaves that exist only in 2027.11.
results.finding: Both readers met release numbers before the chapter introduces them. Flow A: 'These version numbers are the chapter's real Veldmark releases, but they appear here before the reader knows that.' Flow B (item 8): 'the numbers looked like references I had missed'. Use a generic example or say they are Veldmark's releases.

results.draft_locus: Category Migrations: Splits, Merges, Moves and Retirements ¶5
results.quote: A split that makes battery capacity mandatory for 200,000 existing e-bike listings on day one would block every one of their sellers from changing a price.
results.finding: Flow A: 'The figure reads like a Veldmark number, but the bikes section never says how many listings went to E-bikes. I could not tell whether it was real or illustrative.' results.draft_locus: In Practice: The Bikes Split at Veldmark ¶1 and ¶8
results.quote: It was the first release to go through the new taxonomy service, and it doubled as the first harmonization step for the four Tradeyard trees.
results.finding: Both readers lost the thread most here. Flow A: 'If 2027.10 was the canonical tree's first release, how is 2027.11 the first release through the service?... I could not reconcile the sequence of the two releases.' Flow B (item 13): 'Now a release from before the split already turns each country tree into a view over a canonical tree. I could not tell whether harmonization came before or after the bikes split. The sequence also jumps from November to the December Fatbikes request and then back to October.' The contradiction is in the spec itself: p40's controlling idea calls 2027.11 'the first release through the taxonomy service and the first step in harmonizing', while p47's says 'release 2027.10 holds 1,640 canonical leaves' and each country tree became a view over it, and p47 is placed after the December Fatbikes paragraph (p46). The author must decide what 2027.10 was (an initial canonical load before the split, or a later state) and reword p40 and/or p47 (or move the 2027.10 fact earlier) before the draft can be made consistent.

results.finding: Opens on a thought-provoking question (what is a category?) answered two ways, then the Category Straitjacket and a roadmap; none of the weak patterns.
Does not open with 'in conclusion', does not merely restate the thesis, adds no new body evidence; the closing examples are the spec's hand-off teasers.

'Stable IDs, releases that carry their own mapping and a migration runbook move the cost of a change from the tree to the migration: Fatbikes took two days. Lead time for a new category is the measure to watch.' No single section states this; it gives the so-what.

The intro reader predicted the scene, controls, structure, versioned releases, external mappings, prediction, migrations, the bikes split with harmonization, the four closing sections and the hand-off, in order, with public eBay/Amazon/Google/Shopify/Mercari evidence and fictional Veldmark examples, matching the expected answer.

Reader names the versioned release (2027.11) with tree, default-child mapping, attribute diff and effective dates; reclassification by rules, model above 0.92 and sellers behind a 95% audit gate; saved searches rewritten to the union, 301 redirects, partner codes accepted with warnings, search mappings and models updated, analytics mapping view, local labels and Polish navigation.

Reader names the Category Straitjacket (category treated as content but behaving as a schema key, IDs/names/slugs hard-coded, country trees multiply it) and the fix: one canonical tree with stable meaningless IDs, rules reading properties from the service, navigation/labels/slugs derived, versioned releases consumers pin, and lead time measured.

Reader explains merge has one destination per listing while a split's from-to mapping names only a default, describes Mercari's LLM labelling of several million items among ~10 generated candidates propagated by kNN over embeddings including the original category, and states that no accuracy figure was published.
Reader chooses an attribute (electric assist on Cargo bikes, cargo wins over electric) by the contract rule and names it an additive change cleared by taxonomy team review in two days.
